penalties.reason: Reactive unfolding of steps during execution is not bound to the DA09/DA04 validation pipeline in the test; safety-verification gap on dynamically generated nodes.

atoms.reason: Tri-source consensus and the architectural backbone of the planner — high correctness and impact. But 'reactive unfolding' directly tensions with DA09's prohibition on executing unverified steps (high-impact conflict). Accept the hierarchical DAG model with the modification that any reactively unfolded node must pass structural validation, skill-compliance, and (where applicable) operator review before execution. Low simplicity due to hierarchical DAG + reactive expansion.

Cornerstone safety invariant: a stateless, advisory orchestration layer that grants no new privileges and routes every proposed action through the existing 5-gate loop (fail-closed, risk-ladder, STOP). Tri-source consensus, no review flags, and it is precisely what neutralizes the autonomy risk introduced by DA01/DA07. Clean and high-leverage — accept as-is.

Tri-source consensus. Deep Vision integration (state summary, affordance map, pre/post-condition verification, stuck diagnosis) is what makes precondition/postcondition gating and recovery meaningful, so it materially reduces blind-execution risk. Feasibility and simplicity are dragged down by high implementation cost and dependence on vision reliability, but no conflicts or review flags — accept.

Explicit per-node contracts (intent, preconditions, allowed tools/skills, declared risk class, observable done-criteria, recovery/retry budget) are highly specific and are the enabling substrate for DA05 risk-gating, DA07 recovery, and DA09 validation. Medium cost/reversibility, no review flags — accept.

Mandatory declared-risk ladder as a confirm-barrier for high-risk actions (e.g. system_mutation), classified at task level and re-checked per node before execution. Tri-source consensus, very high risk-reduction, medium and feasible cost. Re-classification at each node is the right granularity — accept.

Global, asynchronous, preemptive STOP that halts planner, executor, recovery, and pending confirmations with no auto-resume and a partial-state report — a non-negotiable safety invariant with tri-source consensus. Feasibility and simplicity are reduced because correct preemptive async abort across all subsystems is genuinely hard to implement, but correctness and risk-reduction dominate — accept.

penalties.reason: Steps produced by reactive subgraph replanning are not explicitly routed through DA09/DA04 validation before execution (medium-impact conflict with DA09).

atoms.reason: Bounded recovery ladder (retry → re-perceive/vision diagnosis → reactive subgraph replanning → escalate/STOP) is consensus and well-structured, with attempt budgets that prevent runaway loops. Modify: any node generated by reactive replanning must re-enter structural validation, skill-compliance, and (if applicable) operator review before execution, closing the medium-impact conflict with DA09. Low simplicity and feasibility from the high-cost multi-stage mechanism.

Constraining LLM decomposition to the existing closed skill vocabulary (open/type/telegram/vision) with fail-closed escalation on any out-of-vocabulary request is low-cost, high-reversibility, highly specific, and strongly bounds the capability surface. This is the primary guard against the LLM inventing dangerous actions — accept.

penalties.reason: Test covers only initial plan loading and document approval; it does not verify validation/review of dynamically unfolded (DA01) or replanned (DA07) steps.

atoms.reason: Serializable, typed, schema- and skill-validated plans with no execution of unverified steps, plus operator review of PROJECT_PLAN/contract before implementation — the central control/verification gate, very high risk-reduction. Modify: extend the requirement and its test to explicitly cover dynamically generated and replanned steps, resolving the high-impact conflict with DA01 and the medium one with DA07 so 'no unverified execution' holds throughout, not just at load time.

Single-source (B) but no conflicts and clear safety value: an autonomy watchdog with a no-progress detector and global limits (steps, time, risk budget) that forces a fail-closed stop with report. Complements STOP (DA06) and recovery budgets (DA07) by bounding total autonomous runtime; medium and feasible cost — accept.

Process atom: DISCUSS_* docs must compare and justify the planning-model choice (LLM-only vs rule/task-graph vs hybrid). Low cost, high reversibility, very simple, and it de-risks the architecture decision indirectly by forcing explicit rationale. Impact and direct risk-reduction are modest since it is documentation rather than a runtime control — accept.

penalties.reason: Framed as optional/'consider' with a future-implementation test; under-specified scope and unclear feasibility of dry-run simulation for GUI actions.

atoms.reason: An optional PLANNER-CRITIC / dry-run simulator would add valuable pre-operator safety screening, but it is single-source, explicitly speculative ('рассмотреть', for future implementation), high-cost, and hard to build credibly for GUI-level actions. Modify: keep as a deferred, scoped enhancement (e.g. static lint of the TaskGraph against schema/skills/risk first; full dry-run later) rather than a committed near-term deliverable. Lowest total — accept only as a future track.
